Clause fields (authentication/authorization/confidentiality/integrity/revocation/audit) state what a crossing's control REQUIRES; they are a charter, not a report. `deliveryStatus` is the separate field that says whether the control has actually been built and measured -- delivered | partial | not-delivered | unaudited -- and `deliveryEvidence` carries the backing. `partial` (added by W20) means the crossing HAS been audited and its asserted clauses split: at least one is enforced by a named line that was exhibited denying, and at least one is absent; it is NOT a softer `delivered` and must never be read as one. Like `not-delivered` it must cite a live finding id, so the absent half is always owned by something a census can see. Before this field the two were indistinguishable, and a Critical crossing measured absent read exactly like one that holds. `unaudited` is the honest default for a crossing nobody has audited; it must never be upgraded to `delivered` except from a recorded measurement.
